subject: Proposal: stepped prepay schedule to cap price increases
messages:

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal question — price increases and multi-year option

Hi Laura,

Quick one as we kick off renewal planning for Q4: our contract with Redwood is up for renewal and we're seeing public list increases in a number of vendors this year. I'd rather lock a predictable cost for our forecasting. Do you have a multi-year prepay option that would both: (a) let us lock current unit pricing, and (b) give us a step-down discount if we commit more volume upfront?

If so, we could look at a 2–3 year prepay with a modest ramp in committed usage year-over-year. Happy to take a short call, but if you can share typical structures/discount bands upfront that helps procurement.

Thanks,
Matt

Apex Analytics

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal question — price increases and multi-year option

Hi Matt — thanks for the note. We do offer multi-year prepay options designed precisely for customers who want predictable unit economics and protection from list increases. High level options we typically present: 

- 1-year annual prepay: modest discount off list, flexible true-up quarterly.
- 2-year prepay with flat price lock: larger upfront discount in exchange for 2x commitment; optional step-downs in year 2.
- 3-year stepped prepay: biggest discount in year 1 (higher upfront payment), then planned step-down reductions as you hit usage bands (designed to reward growth).

I can put together a draft step-down schedule (example %s per year + ramp assumptions) and loop in finance for formal pricing. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk through a term sheet? If you prefer I’ll send a draft term sheet first.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc:  
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Apex renewal — draft structure thoughts

Folks — looping you in. Apex (Matthew) is asking about locking pricing to avoid vendor list increases. They sign ~$1.1M ARR today, with expected 10–20% growth next 12 months. Proposal idea (draft):

- Term: 3 years prepaid (annual invoicing but paid upfront each year or full prepay permitted)
- Year 1: 20% discount off published unit price for committed tokens; minimum floor equals 0.9x current annual usage
- Year 2: 15% discount; commitment increases by +10% over prior year (ramped usage band)
- Year 3: 10% discount; commitment assumes steady-state +10% over Year 2
- True-ups: quarterly true-up for usage above committed bands; no refunds for under-usage but credits apply if you prepay full term
- Price protection: if public list increases, customer's unit price remains capped at the contracted unit price for term

Finance, can you flag whether 20/15/10 is doable from a margin/approval standpoint? Also suggest any required guardrails (minimum ARR floor, clawbacks, early termination language). I can send a client-facing term sheet once we align.

Thanks,
Laura

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Apex renewal — draft structure thoughts

Laura — thanks for the write-up. A few internal thoughts:

- 20/15/10 looks generous relative to typical mid-market prepay tiers. I'd suggest 18% / 13% / 8% to preserve unit economics, with the option to increase Year 1 to 20% if Apex prepays >= 1.5x ARR (i.e., larger upfront commitment).
- Require a minimum ARR floor equal to 0.8x current ARR for discount to remain in effect; if usage drops below that floor for two consecutive quarters, discount steps down by 5 percentage points.
- Add an annual escalation cap on list price impact we absorb — e.g., we will cap customer unit price increases to +3% year-over-year (from their contracted unit price) even if public list jumps more. That tradeoff helps us manage long-term margin risk.
- For ramp, define clear bands and quarterly true-ups. Also recommend including a clause to allow Redwood to re-evaluate discounts if usage variance > 30% vs committed baseline.

If these look reasonable I can prepare a one-page internal term sheet and a customer-facing draft.

Thanks,
Aditya
Director, Revenue Operations

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Apex renewal — draft structure thoughts

Agree with Aditya's adjusted bands and gate conditions. A few controls from the finance/sales leadership side: 

- Approve 18/13/8 baseline; allow stretch to 20/15/10 only with VP-level signoff and proof of prepayment >= 1.5x ARR or multi-year banked payment.
- Include an Under-Utilization Remediation clause: if actual billed usage < 75% of committed usage for two consecutive quarters, we reserve right to accelerate billing or reduce discount retroactively (limited to 5% adjustment).
- Require a minimum non-refundable deposit equal to 25% of Year 1 prepay for execution (applies to all multi-year deals > $500k).
- Contractual Price Protection: commit to capping customer unit price increases at 3% YoY for the term — we will absorb larger public list changes up to a capped exposure; any extraordinary third-party hardware cost inflation (>8% YoY) will be subject to re-opener.
- Compliance: procurement will ask for SOC2 and data handling attestation. Please attach the SOC2 cert to the external term sheet.

Once you share the client-facing draft, I'll give final approval and signoff language.

— Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposed stepped prepay term sheet (draft) — Apex Analytics renewal

Matt — thanks again for the conversation last week. Attached is a draft term sheet and an example stepped prepay schedule that reflects the internal guidance from Finance. High-level summary: 

- Term: 3 years, annual prepaid invoices (full-term prepay optional)
- Discount bands: Year 1 = 18% (20% if full prepay >=1.5x ARR), Year 2 = 13%, Year 3 = 8%
- Ramp: committed usage bands increase by +10% YoY; quarterly true-up with credits for over-usage; no refunds for under-usage (credits apply if full-term prepay)
- Price protection: your unit price will be capped at contracted price + max 3% YoY during the term (we will absorb public list increases up to that cap)
- Minimums & deposit: 25% non-refundable Year 1 deposit for any multi-year prepay > $500k; minimum ARR floor 0.8x current ARR to keep discounts in place
- Guardrails: Under-utilization remediation and re-opener for extraordinary hardware inflation (>8% YoY)

Attachments: Apex_Renewal_Draft_20260907.pdf (term sheet, client-facing) and redwood_prepaid_term_sheet.xlsx (detailed stepdown schedule and sample invoices). Also attaching our SOC2 attestation as requested in procurement.

Next steps: please review and let me know any procurement questions. If this looks directionally correct, we can issue a DocuSign by Sep 20 to meet your internal renewal timeline. I'll set up a follow-up call for Thursday if that works.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Enterprise Sales
